use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads maintenance logs and equipment manuals to extract key maintenance requirements, inspection intervals, and common failure patterns, then compares current equipment status against scheduled maintenance thresholds.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the dependency on physical inspection by systematizing what should be inspected and when based on documented patterns, allowing technicians to prioritize high-risk items and catch early warning signs before they force unplanned downtime.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Provides structured guidance to technicians on what to inspect, reducing miss-rates versus ad-hoc physical inspection alone.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control by reducing unplanned downtime and extends asset life; critical in a supply distribution business.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Maintenance logs are available but vary in completeness; equipment manuals are structured but may require manual digitization.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires custom extraction of semi-structured maintenance logs and manual content, plus threshold logic; moderate complexity.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Technicians still perform hands-on inspection and repair; this only improves their planning, so adoption risk is low.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No mature off-the-shelf solution for equipment-manual-guided extraction specific to forklift fleets.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal equipment maintenance planning with no profiling of people or regulated decisions.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data is involved; only equipment and maintenance records.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that queries parts inventory in real time and recommends optimal parts to stage before each scheduled maintenance visit, based on historical failure patterns and current stock levels.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses parts availability delays by proactively surfacing which parts are needed, in stock, or should be reordered before maintenance is scheduled, reducing technician wait time and rescheduling.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Avoids repeat visits and technician idle time by ensuring parts are ready; measurably higher first-pass completion rate.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces operational friction and schedule conflicts, directly improving warehouse efficiency and cost per maintenance cycle.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Inventory systems and maintenance logs are structured and readily available; data quality is typically high in distribution operations.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: API integration to inventory system plus pattern matching on historical parts usage; straightforward for a modern platform.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Technicians receive a recommendation they can act on; minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Inventory query and recommendation logic are commodity features in ERP and inventory management tools.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal supply-chain optimization with no profiling or regulated decisions.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data involved.

process: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that reads prior review scores, manager narrative comments, and HR calibration notes, then generates a structured performance summary and suggests consistent scoring tiers (exceeds, meets, needs improvement) for each competency, flagging outliers for HR review.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the wide variation in manager write-up quality and tone by normalizing the input data into a consistent structure before the manager finalizes the review. HR retains full control over the calibration output and can override all suggestions. This improves consistency without removing human judgment.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Normalizes inconsistent manager inputs into structured competency summaries, reducing tone and quality variance.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports HR's operational efficiency and consistency in a high-stakes compliance area (performance reviews).
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Prior scores, narratives, and calibration notes are well-structured, existing HR system data.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Text summarization and rule-based tier suggestion is a standard pattern; integration with HR systems is straightforward.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Managers and HR see the tool as a draft aid they review and edit, not a decision-maker, so adoption is low friction.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several HR platforms (Workday, BambooHR, etc.) and standalone tools already offer performance-drafting assistants.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Limited risk: the tool advises on performance tiers but HR and managers make all final decisions; no automated action or employment decision.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive personal performance and competency data; must remain confidential and subject to data retention policies.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: A classifier that tags manager narratives with common performance themes (e.g., technical excellence, collaboration, missed deadlines, development needs) to accelerate HR's calibration meeting preparation and cross-employee comparison.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the time-consuming calibration meeting prep by pre-tagging narratives with consistent performance dimensions, allowing HR to quickly group similar performance patterns and anomalies across the 60 monthly reviews, without requiring manual narrative re-reading.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces manual rereading and grouping effort; tags may occasionally miss nuance, but HR still validates all groupings.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves calibration meeting efficiency, a secondary but real operational priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Manager narrative text is rich and available; tagging is not dependent on structured fields.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Multi-label text classification on a stable set of performance themes is a proven, low-complexity task.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR uses the tags as a starting point for grouping; they remain the arbiter of final groupings and comparisons.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Pre-trained text classifiers and many HR platforms offer narrative tagging capabilities.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Limited risk: classification is a data-preparation aid that HR reviews and can override; no automated employment decision.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive performance narratives; tags remain within HR confidentiality controls.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An AI tool that extracts and standardizes key policy terms (coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, renewal dates) from current policies and broker quotes, presenting them in a structured comparison table.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the manual comparison of quotes across brokers by automatically pulling and normalizing the critical terms so the procurement team can compare apples-to-apples without re-reading dense legal language.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Eliminates transcription errors and inconsistent interpretation of quote terms, reducing the risk of oversight.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports cost control and procurement efficiency, a core priority for a distribution business.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Policy and quote documents exist but vary in format; extraction accuracy may vary by broker template.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Document extraction with predefined field mapping is well-established; some template variance handling needed.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Procurement team still reviews and decides; the tool simply pre-populates a comparison sheet.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several insurance-focused document extraction tools and procurement platforms offer this capability.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal procurement automation with no personal data profiling or sensitive decision-making.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; this is commercial contract and asset data only.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves and summarizes relevant claims history, prior coverage gaps, and asset value trends from internal records to surface risk context before the renewal meeting with brokers.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the complexity of policy terms and the rushed timeline by pre-assembling the internal data the team needs to make an informed renewal decision, reducing the time spent hunting through records mid-renewal.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Provides consistent, complete historical context without cherry-picking; modest improvement in decision quality.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports informed procurement decisions and risk management, secondary but important.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Claims history and asset inventory are structured internal records, readily available and reliable.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Query and summarization logic against existing databases; straightforward integration.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Zero workflow disruption; the team simply receives a pre-prepared briefing document.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No commodity tool covers this specific internal context retrieval; custom build on existing data stores.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal risk context assembly with no algorithmic decision-making.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Touches claims history which may contain employee injury or operational incident details indirectly.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves order history, verifies purchase date against return policy windows, and surfaces condition requirements to the agent in real-time during live chat.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the pain of agents checking multiple systems to verify purchase date and condition. By surfacing the relevant data and policy windows in one place, the assistant reduces lookup time and ensures agents have consistent information to make decisions.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: By surfacing order history and policy windows consistently, agents make faster decisions with less risk of overlooking eligibility rules.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces chat handling time and improves customer satisfaction by faster resolution, both customer service priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Order history and purchase dates are structured and readily available in the ERP/order management system.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires API integration to order and policy systems, plus chat embedding, but no custom ML—a standard retrieval pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agent workflow remains unchanged; the tool simply puts information at their fingertips instead of making them hunt across systems.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No mature off-the-shelf solution fully handles this integration with live chat; custom build needed.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal customer-service workflow tool, no recruitment, credit, or access decisions—minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses customer purchase history and order data, which is indirectly personal but not sensitive (not health, biometric, etc.).

use_cases.description: A classifier trained on historical return decisions that flags return requests as clearly-eligible, clearly-ineligible, or needs-agent-judgment based on purchase date, product condition, and policy rules.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses inconsistent return decisions across agents and the high volume of repetitive eligibility questions. By flagging routine cases, the classifier helps agents triage faster and reduces decision variance.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies policy consistently to routine cases, reducing decision variance, though edge cases still require agent judgment.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves consistency and reduces average handling time, supporting operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Requires labeled historical decisions (purchase date, condition, outcome) which may exist but may need cleaning and labeling.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard supervised classification on structured fields; moderate build effort for model training and integration.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents must trust and act on classifier confidence scores; some re-training needed but not a major workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No pre-built classifier for industrial returns policy; custom model required.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Classification of return eligibility is not a regulated decision (no recruitment, credit, education, law enforcement)—minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses historical order and product condition data tied to customers, indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads bank statements (PDF or image) and automatically extracts transaction details (date, amount, description, reference codes) into structured data, matching them against general ledger line items by amount, date, and reference fields.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the core pain point: manual matching of thousands of transactions is the most time-consuming and error-prone step. Automating extraction and initial matching cuts the time spent on routine, high-volume, repetitive transaction lookups, while the finance team retains full control over exception handling and final reconciliation sign-off.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies consistent extraction logic to every transaction; human reviewers catch edge cases and exceptions, reducing missed or mismatched items.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports close deadline pressure and cost control by cutting manual transaction matching time, a material back-office efficiency.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Bank statements are structured PDFs or images; GL transactions are already in ERP systems as clean, structured data.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Bank statement OCR and rule-based fuzzy matching on amount/date/reference is a mature, low-risk pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Finance team workflow remains largely the same—they review and approve the matches—so adoption friction is low.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several mature reconciliation tools and banking-API integrations already provide this capability.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal financial reconciliation with no profiling of employees or external parties; minimal regulatory risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Touches transaction and GL data, some of which may reference employee expense codes or vendor details; classified as indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: A classifier that flags unmatched transactions as likely timing differences (outstanding checks, deposits-in-transit, fees, or interest), probable posting errors, or true discrepancies requiring manual investigation.
use_cases.justification: After extraction and initial matching, most unmatched items are routine timing or posting issues. Triaging them automatically reduces the finance team's investigation time and increases confidence that they are focusing only on genuinely anomalous discrepancies, ensuring zero-tolerance error control is maintained under deadline pressure.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies consistent categorization rules to every unmatched item, reducing fatigue-driven oversight; humans still verify each finding.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports close deadline and zero-error tolerance by prioritizing high-risk discrepancies.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Uses structured matched/unmatched transaction data from the extraction step, plus clean GL history.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Rule-based or simple ML classifier on transaction metadata (amount, date, description patterns) is low effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Minimal; finance team simply reviews the triage output before investigation, no workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Reconciliation triage logic is a commodity feature in modern accounting tools.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal transaction triage with no external profiling; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses the same indirectly personal transaction and GL data as the extraction step.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that reads an approved content item and its platform guidelines, then auto-generates the platform-specific post copy, hashtags, and scheduling metadata for each target platform, ready for the marketing team to review and schedule.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of manually copying approved content into each platform's scheduler. By generating platform-optimized versions from a single source creative, it eliminates repetitive manual reformatting while keeping humans in control of the final scheduling decision.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Generates consistent, platform-compliant posts from one source, reducing manual errors, though tone/brand fit still needs human review.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves marketing team efficiency but is not tied to revenue, customer acquisition, or compliance priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approved content, platform guidelines, and calendar structure are well-structured and readily available.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Prompt-based generation with simple parameter injection; standard LLM task with no custom modeling required.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Marketing team must still review and approve before scheduling, so minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several social media management platforms (Buffer, Hootsuite, Later) already offer AI-assisted post composition.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Generates outbound marketing content with no profiling, decision-making, or risk to individuals; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data is processed; purely internal content optimization.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads the approval sign-offs and content metadata, then tags each calendar item as approved, pending-review, or rejected, automatically updating the tracking status visible to the team.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain point of tracking which posts are pending versus published. By automatically ingesting approval records and updating status, it eliminates the manual overhead of status updates and gives the team real-time visibility into the pipeline without duplicating approvals.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Removes manual status entry, so consistency and accuracy of the tracking record improve significantly.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves internal workflow visibility but does not support revenue or cost control.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approval sign-offs may come via email, Slack, or forms; not all are structured, requiring some normalization.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on approval metadata and sign-off text; moderate logic required to parse varied approval formats.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Status updates become automatic; minimal change to how the team approves content, only how status is tracked.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Most commercial social schedulers do not auto-ingest approval workflows; custom logic needed.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal status tracking for marketing content; no profiling or regulated decision-making.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processing; only content and approval metadata.

use_cases.description: An AI classifier that assigns severity level (critical, high, medium, low) to incoming IT support tickets based on ticket description, system logs, and historical incident patterns.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the inconsistent severity categorization pain point by applying uniform severity rules to every ticket submission, reducing manual judgment variance and ensuring critical issues are properly surfaced.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies consistent severity logic to every ticket, reducing human variance and catching genuinely critical issues that might be under-categorized.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces mean time to resolution for high-impact incidents by ensuring proper prioritization.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket descriptions, logs, and incident history are structured and already captured in the ticketing system.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard text classification with structured log features; well-established pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Classifier output is a recommendation; engineers still review and can override, so minimal workflow disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: ITSM platforms (ServiceNow, Jira) and standalone severity classifiers already exist for this.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal operational triage with no personal data profiling.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; ticket contents and logs contain only system/technical information.

use_cases.description: An AI-powered search and matching assistant that identifies duplicate or related tickets by comparing the new ticket description against historical incident records and currently open tickets, surfacing potential matches for the on-call engineer to review.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the duplicate-ticket detection pain point and reduces the time on-call engineers spend manually searching for related incidents, allowing faster consolidation and routing of work.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistently surfaces duplicate and related tickets that manual scanning would miss, reducing duplicate effort.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves support team efficiency and reduces toil, supporting operational excellence.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Incident history and current ticket database are well-structured and readily accessible.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Similarity matching and semantic search are commodity capabilities in modern ITSM tools.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Engineers must still validate and act on matches; it is a lookup aid, not a forced action.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: ITSM platforms and ticket management tools have built-in deduplication and similarity features.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal ticket matching and deduplication with no personal data processing.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; compares technical incident descriptions only.

use_cases.description: An AI classifier that reads sales transactions and commission plan rules to flag transactions as standard-tier, exception-tier (by region/product), or requires-manual-review, categorizing them before calculation.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the error-prone manual spreadsheet calculations and rep disputes by consistently applying the complex region/product-line exception rules upfront, reducing miscalculations before they reach payroll.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies exception rules consistently across all reps and regions, eliminating the spreadsheet errors that fuel disputes.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces payroll errors and rep friction, directly supporting operational efficiency and employee satisfaction in a high-stakes process.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Sales transactions and commission rules are structured, transactional data that is clean and readily available.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Classification on well-defined rule categories is straightforward; custom training on historical dispute patterns can improve accuracy.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Sales Ops still reviews and approves flagged cases before payroll, so workflow remains similar; reps see transparent, auditable categorization.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: No commodity tool covers the nuanced region/product-line exception logic specific to NordIndus; custom classifier required.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal compensation calculation with no profiling or discrimination risk; minimal regulatory exposure.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes employee sales and territory data (indirectly personal) but no sensitive health or demographic data.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves and summarizes the commission plan rules, rep territory assignments, and applicable exceptions for a given transaction or rep, allowing Sales Ops staff to quickly verify calculations and resolve disputes with reps.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the payroll deadline pressure and disputes by giving Sales Ops near-instant access to the specific rules and exceptions that apply to a transaction, reducing time spent hunting through documents and validating why a calculation was made.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Speeds rule lookup and reference but does not change calculation logic; modest consistency gain from faster access to authoritative rules.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces time pressure and enables faster dispute resolution, supporting operational efficiency and rep retention.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Commission plans and territory assignments are structured documents; retrieval is straightforward.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over structured commission documents is a mature pattern; minimal custom work.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Sales Ops staff simply ask questions instead of searching; natural workflow improvement with no disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: LLM-based assistant with RAG (e.g., OpenAI API, internal LLM + vector store) is a commodity capability.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Retrieval and summarization of internal policy; no decision-making or profiling.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Accesses employee territory and sales data but only for reference, not profiling or automated decision-making.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that ingests onboarding documents (contracts, ID, tax forms) submitted via email, portal, or message and automatically extracts key fields (name, ID number, tax ID, start date, role, employment type) and maps them against the compliance checklist to identify missing or incomplete submissions.
use_cases.justification: This directly addresses the pain of manual checklist-against-document checking and the multiple disconnected submission channels by consolidating intake, extracting structured data once, and flagging gaps before HR reviews.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Applies the compliance checklist consistently to every submission, catching missing documents or incomplete fields that manual review might skip.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports compliance and system access speed, reducing onboarding delays and HR manual toil.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Employment contracts, ID images, and tax forms are structured or semi-structured; the checklist is a fixed document.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: OCR plus field extraction and checklist matching is well-established; integration to HR systems may add complexity.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR still reviews and approves; the tool replaces manual form-checking, so workflow change is modest.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document-extraction and onboarding OCR tools already exist in the HR tech market.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal HR process with no profiling, credit, or access decisions made autonomously; extraction only.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes sensitive personal data: ID numbers, tax IDs, employment terms, right-to-work status. Requires secure handling and retention policies.

use_cases.description: A classifier that prioritizes onboarding cases by readiness: ready-for-access (all docs present and valid), needs-follow-up (missing docs, low-confidence extractions), or escalate (conflicting or suspicious data). HR acts on the prioritization to fast-track ready cases to IT provisioning.
use_cases.justification: This unblocks the start-of-work system access bottleneck by allowing HR to immediately route complete submissions to IT, rather than waiting for all submissions to be manually reviewed in serial order.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces manual review overhead; classification is based on extraction results, so accuracy depends on extraction quality.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly shortens time-to-access, a key pain point that affects employee productivity and compliance reporting.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Operates on structured extraction outputs from the first use case, clean and consistent input.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: A simple prioritization classifier on extracted fields, low build effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR workflow shifts slightly to work in priority order, but no approval gate changes; minimal friction.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Rule-based triage on structured fields is commodity; can be built as a simple decision layer in existing HR tools.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal HR triage based on document completeness, not profiling or automated access decisions.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Operates on the same sensitive personal data, but only to triage; no new data disclosed or retained beyond the first use case.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that processes inspection checklists and site photos to automatically extract structured hazard data (type, location, severity, evidence) from inspectors' free-text notes and images, populating a standardized hazard database.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the inconsistency in inspector notes by enforcing uniform data capture across all inspections. Structured output enables reliable cross-site hazard analysis without manual re-reading of past reports.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardizes hazard capture across inspectors and sites, eliminating gaps and inconsistencies in reporting.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Safety compliance and risk management are core to industrial distribution; structured hazard data is essential for regulatory reporting and loss prevention.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Inspection checklists are structured; site photos and notes are available but unstructured—OCR and vision models handle this well.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: OCR on forms plus image object detection (cracks, exposed hazards, etc.) is a well-established pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Inspectors fill in forms and take photos as usual; extraction happens downstream, minimal workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document extraction and construction-site image analysis tools exist (e.g., from safety-tech vendors).
criteria_rationale.ai_act: No personal data profiling; internal safety data extraction is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data is processed; only hazard and site data.

use_cases.description: A classifier that identifies recurring hazard patterns across all logged inspections (e.g., 'electrical hazards at Site A', 'fall risk in multi-story work') and flags sites or asset types with disproportionately high hazard frequency for proactive intervention.
use_cases.justification: Directly solves the pain point of manually cross-referencing past reports to spot trends. Automated pattern detection enables faster root-cause identification and resource allocation to high-risk sites.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Spots hazard clusters humans would miss in manual scanning; enables data-driven prioritization of corrective actions.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Risk analytics and proactive safety planning are critical in industrial distribution and reduce liability and losses.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Builds on the structured hazard data from extraction; classified logs provide high-quality training signal.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Pattern matching and clustering on structured hazard fields is straightforward; can use rule-based or simple ML.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Generates reports for safety managers; does not change inspector or site supervisor workflows.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Clustering and anomaly detection are commodity ML capabilities; many EHSS (Environmental, Health, Safety) platforms offer this.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: No personal profiling; aggregate safety analytics on site and hazard data is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; only aggregated hazard and site data.

use_cases.description: An AI assistant that retrieves open corrective actions from the logs, matches them to newly logged hazards, reminds safety managers of overdue closures, and suggests which open actions might resolve newly identified recurring hazards.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the lack of automatic tracking to completion. Assistant provides visibility into which corrective actions are in progress, overdue, or applicable to newly discovered hazards, reducing manual follow-up effort.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Improves visibility of overdue actions; matching suggestions reduce redundant corrective action creation but rely on safety manager judgment.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Ensures corrective actions are executed, supporting compliance and audit trails, which are high priorities in regulated industrial work.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Corrective action logs are structured; matching uses the extracted hazard data, which is now standardized.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Retrieval and matching on structured fields plus deadline alerts is low complexity; can use rule-based logic and simple NLP.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Safety managers receive alerts and suggestions but retain full control; minimal process disruption.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Reminder and cross-reference tools are built into most EHSS software; no custom development required.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: No personal profiling; internal tracking of corrective actions is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: No personal data processed; only action and hazard logs.
